subject: Ref identity/printed type: RULED s320 — referent-kind tag on the box APPROVED, first POST-R1 runtime item (also fixes #154's two shapes)
description:
DONE s333.  NO ref-kind SLOT was added — see docs/DECIDED.md §s333 and
docs/opus5-review-requests-s333.md §1 (deviation from the s318/s320 ruling, flagged for confirmation).

WHAT THE "THIRD STORAGE PATH" TURNED OUT TO BE: not a third representation, a second CALLER LEVEL.
A reference reaches a stringifier either as a variable box holding the p-backslash wrapper
(`my $r = \$x`) or AS THE WRAPPER (`\$x` into print / an element / a p-raw-params parameter /
the eager %pcl-to-string-strict slot).  box-sv guessed by COUNTING BOXES, so one reference
printed SCALAR at one level and REF at the other.  p-ref never had the bug — it asks
(p-box-is-ref val).  Fix = CLAUDE.md 11: one %p-ref-referent, read by box-sv,
stringify-value, box-nv, p-ref and overload::StrVal.

FIXED (all measured against perl, both directions):
- identity/address: was the WRAPPER's (fresh per `\`), so `\$x == \$x` was false and one
  variable printed two addresses; now the referent's.
- ref(\$aref)/(\$href)/(\$cref)/(\$qr) answered ARRAY/HASH/REF/REGEXP; perl says REF.
- `\5` printed REF; `\$vstring` printed SCALAR (perl: VSTRING).
- a ref's string was sv-CACHED, so the dynamic SCALAR<->REF rule could not fire
  (`my $r=\1; my $rr=\$r;` stayed REF after `$r=5`).  Refs are no longer cached — the word
  depends on a DIFFERENT box.  Cost flagged in the review doc §2.
- #154's two shapes closed: @$sref / %$sref / $sref->{k} / $sref->[0] are perl's fatal on
  BOTH read and write paths (%p-scalar-referent-p).  Each check sits behind a p-box-p guard
  so the hot deref paths are unchanged.

FILED #211: `$$refref->{k}` and `${$rr}->{k}` both emit `(p-gethash-deref $rr "k")` — the outer
deref level is DROPPED at parse.  That is what forced #154's "a leftover box is not a mismatch"
leniency, which is why the ref-to-REF half stays lenient until #211 lands.

GATES: Pl/t PASS 130 files / 4567 (HEAD 4547 + the 20 rows of the new Pl/t/ref-identity-01.t,
six of them INVERSE guards).  Full sweep run twice: run 1 NOT CLEAN on `LOST ref.t -5`, run 2
(same tree) CLEAN with ref.t 186+18, TOTAL 18469 -> 18475, 0 new / 2 fixed (scalar.t).  ref.t
alone is 186+18 deterministically and HEAD-in-a-worktree is 184+20, so the change is +2 and
run 1 was load noise (23 fresh_perl children) — gate-policy ask in the review doc §4.
